title: When the Locker Falls
premise: In the fading mill town of Halloway, Coral Hartwell has survived seven years of high school by being invisible — until her history teacher pairs her with Eli Vance, the golden-boy quarterback who has made her life miserable since freshman year. Their assignment: document the demolition of the school's original 1948 gymnasium lockers, which turns out to hold a hidden cache belonging to Danny Okafor, a student erased from the town's records in 1954 after he accused the founding family of a deadly cover-up. As Coral and Eli dig into Danny's letters, they uncover how the Vance dynasty buried the truth — and how Eli's family name is stitched through it. Falling for each other forces both of them to choose between the safety of their old labels and the dangerous freedom of who they might be. In the end, they publish Danny's story the night the lockers come down, Coral comes out on her own terms, and the town must finally remember what it chose to forget.
about_author: Sebastian Lockridge is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent three years covering school board meetings in a community of under a thousand people. They write young adult fiction about the secrets small places keep and the kids brave enough to dig them up.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Establishes Halloway's claustrophobia: Coral's seven-year routine of careful silence, her best friend Priya, and the way she edits herself sentence by sentence. Ends with the history teacher announcing semester partners. Beat: weary resignation cracked open by dread.

chapters.title: Nemesis, Assigned
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She's paired with Eli Vance, who once spread a rumor that got her shoved into the creek. Their first meeting is all barbed politeness; he's strangely distracted, snapping at her when she mentions the gym demolition. Beat: hostile friction with an undertow of something unreadable.

chapters.title: Rust and Numbers
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral/Eli POV. Surveying the condemned 1948 gym, Eli goes pale at locker 117. Coral notices. He lies badly about why. She starts a private list of his inconsistencies. Beat: the first hairline crack in her picture of him.

chapters.title: The Yearbook With a Page Missing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the library, Coral finds the 1954 yearbook with a razor-bladed gap where one student's photo should be. The librarian, Mrs. Okafor — Danny's niece — goes silent and shuts the archive room. Beat: the thrill of an open door that should have stayed shut.

chapters.title: Truce Terms
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli, working alone at night, admits to himself he's known about locker 117 since his grandfather's deathbed ramblings. He proposes a truce to Coral: they finish the project clean, no digging. Coral, sensing fear rather than malice, agrees — for now. Beat: uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: Locker 117 Won't Open
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The district fast-tracks demolition for homecoming weekend. Coral and Eli photograph the gym; locker 117 is welded from the inside. Eli touches it like a grave. Coral catches him mouthing a name. Beat: shared secret forming against both their wills.

chapters.title: What Eli's Grandfather Kept
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli finds his grandfather's lockbox: a 1954 coroner's report, a bribe ledger, and a photo of Danny Okafor alive beside a boy who looks exactly like Eli's father. The Vances didn't just witness the cover-up — they built it. Beat: inherited guilt made concrete.

chapters.title: Creek Water and Honest Words
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. After a demolition-delay protest fails, Eli finds Coral crying at the creek where the old rumor started. He apologizes — specifically, in detail, having clearly rehearsed it for years. Something shifts. Beat: the rumor's author dismantling his own weapon.

chapters.title: The Letters of Danny Okafor
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Mrs. Okafor, moved by their persistence, gives them Danny's letters hidden in her family Bible: he documented mine-safety bribes that killed three workers, including his own father, and the school erased him for it. Locker 117 is his time capsule. Beat: righteous fury, purpose found.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At homecoming, Eli's father — now a state senator — gives a speech honoring the gym's history and 'the fine Vance legacy.' Eli watches Coral watch him lie, and realizes she's the only person who knows both his names. Beat: love recognized in complicity.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Late night in the gym, cataloguing artifacts, they almost kiss — and Eli pulls away, terrified, saying he can't be 'that guy in this town.' Coral, stung, tells him she's been that girl for seven years and it hasn't killed her. Beat: first real wound between them.

chapters.title: The Senator's Offer
chapters.summary: Alternating. Senator Vance summons them both: a full-ride fund for their college dreams in exchange for a project about 'the gym's proud history.' He knows about the letters. Coral refuses instantly; Eli hesitates three seconds too long. Beat: the corruption theme made personal.

chapters.title: Priya's Question
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Priya confronts Coral: she's spent so long being careful she's forgotten what she actually wants — including whether Eli is worth it. Coral realizes her silence protected no one, least of all herself. Beat: turning the memory theme inward.

chapters.title: What Was Taken From Danny
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Researching Danny's life after Halloway, they learn he died alone in 1971, still writing letters no one answered. Eli understands his grandfather's deathbed guilt at last — and decides the Vances' name isn't worth the price of another erasure. Beat: resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in the Dark
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Eli comes to Coral's house, soaks wet, and tells the truth: he's been hiding the same way she has, just with a jersey instead of silence. They kiss. For one night the labels are off. Beat: tenderness after damage.

chapters.title: The Welder's Torch
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With demolition moved up, they cut locker 117 open at dawn: inside, Danny's full evidence — mine maps, names, and a letter addressed 'to whoever is brave enough.' Also his class ring, which the school registry lists as 'lost.' Beat: the past physically handed over.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. The senator learns the locker is open. Eli's father, complicit and frightened, begs him to stop 'for the family.' Eli chooses. He copies everything and mails a set to the county paper. Beat: open declaration of war on his own name.

chapters.title: When the Locker Falls
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Demolition day. The whole town watches the gym fall; Coral and Eli stand at the front, holding the evidence, as the senator tries to have them escorted away and the crowd — including Mrs. Okafor — closes ranks around the kids instead. Beat: public climax, courage witnessed.

chapters.title: The Story Runs
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The county paper publishes Danny's story with the coroner's report. The senator resigns his committee seats; the school board votes to restore Danny's name to the 1954 record. Coral, interviewed on camera, says the words 'I'm Coral Hartwell, and I live here' out loud, on purpose. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Backlash and Ballast
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. The town splits — some doors close to them, but unexpected allies open others, including the football coach who benches the senator's old trophy from the lobby. Eli quits the team's final season to finish Danny's memorial archive. Beat: cost counted, worth confirmed.

chapters.title: Danny's Name on the Wall
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The school dedicates a plaque and reopens the yearbook page with Danny's photo restored. Mrs. Okafor places his class ring beside it. Coral reads Danny's letter aloud — 'to whoever is brave enough' — and understands it was always addressed to them. Beat: memory repaired.

chapters.title: Who We Are With the Labels Off
chapters.summary: Both POVs, closing. Graduation. Coral and Eli leave Halloway not to escape it but changed by it, driving past the empty lot where the gym stood. Coral's hand in his, out the window, in daylight, in town. Beat: love and truth chosen over safety — the ending earned.
